observation.visible_scene: A young woman with dark hair and prominent eyebrows holds a clear drinking glass that is partly filled with water; a teal straw is inserted and appears visually broken/bent at the waterline (a refraction effect). She faces the camera against a plain yellow wall and is talking throughout the excerpt. Her other hand, holding the glass from below, is partly visible at the bottom, while a second hand enters from the left side of the frame.
visible_changes: The woman's mouth shape changes continuously from frame to frame (closed, slightly open, teeth showing), consistent with ongoing speech.

A hand/index finger first appears at the far-left edge around frame 3 and progressively moves rightward across the segment; by the later frames (roughly 22 onward) the extended fingertip is positioned at the left side of the glass, level with the waterline.
The glass, the water surface, and the teal straw remain essentially fixed in position relative to the woman's face; there is no large translation or deformation of these objects within the excerpt.
The yellow background and the framing of the subject stay roughly constant, indicating no clear camera pan or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: The content of the woman's speech (no audio is available).
Whether the pointing finger actually touches the glass or merely hovers near it.
What precedes the start of the segment and what follows after it (e.g., whether the straw is later moved or removed).
Whether the apparent bend of the straw is being deliberately demonstrated or is incidental.
uncertain_details: Exact point of contact between the fingertip and the glass wall (the tip looks very close but contact is not clearly confirmed).
Any small camera jitter versus genuine hand motion is hard to separate, though the hand's rightward progression is consistent across many frames.
The precise moment the hand begins entering the frame (first faint edge around frame 3).

may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
